statement: A Runtime holds one connection state per socket and nothing else of it: the Runtime with the smaller id dials, once per peer (a peer whose handshake is under way is not dialed again), a line is a handshake step or a sealed record, a message goes to its peer's newest connection that is up, and a message with no connection is dropped and counted, never sent on another peer's.
source: plan/backlog/e2e.md S3 (the Host's peers over sockets); Q-T-4, Q-T-5

layers.arrival: n/a: the Arrival specs run one Runtime's Host core, not the sockets under it
layers.quint: n/a: the Quint model takes the link as a channel that may lose, repeat or reorder; sockets are below it
layers.contract: n/a: connections and timers are off-chain
layers.rig: owed: test rig (a walk predicate for this rule; none is named yet)

killers.name: R-MESH only the Runtime with the smaller id dials, and a peer that is not up is wanted
R-MESH a handshake in lines leaves both ends up, and a closed connection is wanted again
R-MESH a peer whose handshake is under way is not dialed again, and is once its connection closes
R-MESH a message is sealed on the peer's connection, and arrives at the peer's Host from the peer
R-MESH a message for a peer not up, or for an Entity no peer speaks for, is dropped and said
